input.question: If the sensation of pain is there to tell us we have been damaged, why are serious injuries usually accompanied by such crippling pain that we are unable to move/do anything about the injury?
input.ground_truth: The pain is usually there to keep you from moving and making things worse. In an actual emergency the body releasing pain-blocking chemicals that will allow you to ignore the pain so you can do what you need to in order to survive.

Now, if your robot gets a really big boo-boo, the sensors send a super strong "ouch!" message to its brain. This is so the robot stops moving right away and doesn’t make the boo-boo worse. It’s like the robot’s way of saying, “Stop! Don’t move! Let’s fix this before it gets even worse!”

That’s why, when you get a really bad hurt, your body sends you a lot of pain. It’s telling you to STOP and protect yourself so you don’t get hurt even more. Once you’re safe, the pain will start to go away a little, and you can do something about it.
